title: The JavaScript Event Loop
content: JavaScript is single-threaded. The event loop processes: 1) Call Stack (synchronous code), 2) Microtask Queue (Promises, queueMicrotask), 3) Macrotask Queue (setTimeout, setInterval, I/O). Microtasks always run before the next macrotask. `console.log('a'); setTimeout(()=>console.log('b'),0); Promise.resolve().then(()=>console.log('c'))` prints a, c, b.

title: Promises & Async/Await
content: A Promise represents a future value: `new Promise((resolve, reject) => { ... })`. Chain with `.then(val => ...).catch(err => ...)`. `async/await` is syntactic sugar: `async function fetchData() { const res = await fetch(url); return res.json(); }`. Always handle rejections — unhandled promise rejections crash Node.js.

title: Closures
content: A closure is a function that remembers the variables from its lexical scope even when executed outside it. Example: `function counter() { let n=0; return () => ++n; }`. Classic gotcha: `for(var i=0;i<3;i++) setTimeout(()=>console.log(i),0)` logs 3,3,3. Fix with `let` (block scope) or an IIFE: `(function(i){ setTimeout(()=>console.log(i),0); })(i)`.

title: Prototype Chain & Inheritance
content: Every JavaScript object has a `[[Prototype]]` link. `class` syntax is syntactic sugar over prototype-based inheritance. `class Animal { constructor(name){this.name=name} speak(){} }`. `class Dog extends Animal { speak(){ super.speak(); console.log('Woof'); } }`. Check prototype: `Object.getPrototypeOf(dog) === Dog.prototype`.

title: Destructuring, Spread & Rest
content: Array destructuring: `const [a, b, ...rest] = [1,2,3,4]`. Object destructuring: `const { name, age=18 } = person`. Rename: `const { name: fullName } = person`. Spread copies: `const newArr = [...arr, 4]`. `const merged = { ...obj1, ...obj2 }`. Rest collects remaining args: `function sum(first, ...others) {}`.

title: Array Higher-Order Methods
content: `map` transforms: `arr.map(x => x*2)`. `filter` selects: `arr.filter(x => x>0)`. `reduce` folds: `arr.reduce((acc,x) => acc+x, 0)`. `find` returns first match: `arr.find(x => x.id===5)`. `some/every` check conditions. `flat(n)` flattens n levels. `flatMap` maps then flattens one level. Chain these for expressive pipelines.

title: The `this` Keyword
content: `this` depends on call context. In a method: `this` = the object. In a standalone function: `this` = `undefined` (strict) or `globalThis`. Arrow functions capture `this` from enclosing lexical scope — they have no own `this`. Override with `.bind(ctx)`, `.call(ctx, args)`, or `.apply(ctx, [args])`. Common mistake: passing a method as a callback loses its `this`.

title: ES Modules vs CommonJS
content: ESM (modern): `export const fn = () => {}` or `export default fn`. Import: `import { fn } from './mod.js'` or `import fn from './mod.js'`. CommonJS (Node): `module.exports = fn`. `const fn = require('./mod')`. ESM is static (tree-shakeable); CJS is dynamic. In Node.js use `.mjs` extension or `"type":"module"` in package.json for ESM.

title: Error Handling in JavaScript
content: Synchronous: `try { riskyFn() } catch(e) { console.error(e.message) } finally { cleanup() }`. Async: `try { await fetch(url) } catch(e) { ... }` or `.catch(err => ...)`. Custom error: `class AppError extends Error { constructor(msg,code){super(msg);this.code=code} }`. Always add `process.on('unhandledRejection', ...)` in Node.js.

title: DOM Manipulation
content: Select element: `document.querySelector('#id')` or `querySelectorAll('.class')`. Read/write: `el.textContent = 'Hello'`, `el.innerHTML`. Add class: `el.classList.add('active')`. Toggle: `el.classList.toggle('open')`. Listen: `el.addEventListener('click', handler)`. Create: `const div = document.createElement('div'); parent.appendChild(div)`. Remove: `el.remove()`.

title: Fetch API & HTTP Requests
content: GET: `const data = await fetch('/api/users').then(r => r.json())`. POST: `fetch('/api', { method:'POST', headers:{'Content-Type':'application/json'}, body: JSON.stringify(payload) })`. Check status: `if(!res.ok) throw new Error(res.statusText)`. Use `AbortController` for timeouts: `const ctrl = new AbortController(); fetch(url, {signal: ctrl.signal})`.

title: localStorage & sessionStorage
content: `localStorage` persists across sessions. `sessionStorage` clears on tab close. Set: `localStorage.setItem('key', JSON.stringify(val))`. Get: `JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('key'))`. Remove: `localStorage.removeItem('key')`. Clear all: `localStorage.clear()`. Max ~5MB per origin. Do not store sensitive data or tokens.

title: var vs let vs const & Hoisting
content: `var` is function-scoped and hoisted (initialized to `undefined`). `let` and `const` are block-scoped and in the Temporal Dead Zone until their declaration line. `const` prevents reassignment but not mutation of objects/arrays. Always prefer `const` by default, use `let` when reassignment is needed, avoid `var`.

title: JavaScript Performance Tips
content: Debounce: delay execution until after N ms of inactivity (good for search inputs). Throttle: limit execution to once per N ms (good for scroll events). Memoize: cache expensive pure function results. Avoid layout thrashing: batch DOM reads then writes. Use `requestAnimationFrame` for animations. Lazy-load heavy modules with dynamic `import()`.

title: Regular Expressions
content: Create: `/pattern/flags` or `new RegExp('pattern', 'flags')`. Test match: `/\d+/.test(str)`. Extract: `str.match(/\d+/g)`. Replace: `str.replace(/foo/g, 'bar')`. Capture groups: `/(\w+)@(\w+)/`. Named groups: `/(?<user>\w+)@(?<domain>\w+)/`. Common flags: `g` (global), `i` (case-insensitive), `m` (multiline).

title: React Hooks
content: Hooks let you use state and lifecycle methods in functional components. `useState(init)` manages local state. `useEffect(() => { ... return cleanup }, [deps])` runs side-effects. `useMemo(() => val, [deps])` memoizes computed values. `useCallback(fn, [deps])` memoizes callback references. `useRef(init)` stores mutable references that don't trigger re-renders. Rules: only call hooks at the top-level, and only from React function components.

title: Next.js App Router & Components
content: Next.js App Router uses file-system routing under the `app` directory. Files named `page.tsx` define routes. Components are React Server Components (RSC) by default (rendering on the server, zero client bundle size). Add `'use client';` directive at the top of a file to declare a Client Component for interactivity, state, and browser APIs. Use `layout.tsx` for shared page structures.

title: Node.js Streams & Buffers
content: Buffers handle raw binary data in memory: `Buffer.from('hello')`. Streams handle data chunk-by-chunk for memory-efficiency. Readable streams read data: `fs.createReadStream('file.txt')`. Writable streams write data: `fs.createWriteStream('out.txt')`. Duplex/Transform streams do both. Connect them with `.pipe()`: `readable.pipe(transform).pipe(writable)`. Ideal for handling files larger than the memory buffer.
